clue.text: Like some leaves soldier joining army found in new diet

indicators.note: found in says the soldier-and-army pair sits inside the reworked diet letters
new says the letters of diet are made fresh, rearranged into another order
joining says the soldier piece is followed directly by the army piece

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A botanist describes leaves while a soldier signs up for a novel diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like some leaves' is the botanical definition, not a stray phrase; 'new' rearranges the diet letters into DITE, and 'found in' sets the soldier-army pair GITA inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanists call a leaf divided into finger-like lobes, like a hand, by this term.

clue.text: Put out more flags, showing inconsistent principles

definitions.meaning: standards are flags, so twice the standards are more flags
rules applied differently to different people

explanation.definitionFit: Doubling a count of banners, and the hypocrisy of judging others by stricter rules than oneself.

clue.text: Dizzy guy — one theologian for the university

indicators.note: for says one piece takes the place of another in the word

parts.note: guy is a man, taken as written
U is the abbreviation for university
I is the Roman numeral one
DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theologian

explanation.surface: A light-headed fellow trades a divinity scholar for a university.
explanation.walkthrough: In GUY, U (the university) is replaced by I plus DD.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling the head spin; unsteady and light-headed.

clue.text: Go and fish? Pay money to get past this

definitions.text: Pay money to get past this

parts.note: to have a go is to take a turn
pike is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A traveller must pay to get by after going fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: A road with a toll gate where travellers had to pay to proceed.

clue.text: Some patron contributes tip to go in here

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A diner leaves money for staff in a shared pot.
explanation.walkthrough: A tronc is a pool in which restaurant gratuities are collected and shared out among staff.
explanation.definitionFit: The communal fund where restaurant gratuities are pooled for distribution.

clue.text: Maybe like a photo man captures in the morning

indicators.note: captures says the man's name holds the morning abbreviation inside it

parts.note: FRED is a stock man's name
AM, ante meridiem, marks the morning

explanation.surface: A man takes a snapshot early in the day.
explanation.definitionFit: A photograph is often displayed inside a border, so it is mounted that way.

clue.text: Slight polish the second time round?

parts.note: re means again, a second time
to buff is to polish

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether to give a shine another go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slight' is a verb here, to snub, not an adjective meaning small.
explanation.definitionFit: To snub someone is to reject or rebuff them coldly.

clue.text: Unconventional artist stormed in out of control

indicators.note: out of control says the letters run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: An avant-garde painter charged in, raging.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter breaking with tradition in the early twentieth century, rejecting old forms.

clue.text: It's bad news for the countryside as Luddite scheme goes to pot

definitions.text: It's bad news for the countryside

indicators.note: goes to pot, falls to ruin, says the letters are wrecked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A rural plan from technology haters collapses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes to pot' rearranges AS, LUDDITE and SCHEME together.
explanation.definitionFit: A fungal blight that killed millions of British trees from the 1970s, ruining rural landscapes.

clue.text: Almost falls in street on bits from the butcher?

indicators.note: on, in a down clue, says the street piece is placed above the butcher's bits

parts.note: umbles are offal, the innards of a deer

explanation.surface: Someone trips on the pavement over scraps from the meat shop.
explanation.walkthrough: UMBLES, animal entrails, gave us the phrase 'humble pie'.
explanation.definitionFit: Trips and nearly loses footing, without hitting the ground.

clue.text: Perhaps only 10 inches below where you're standing?

definitions.meaning: ten inches is less than twelve, so read as ..., less than a foot
beneath one's feet, on the ground

explanation.definitionFit: Ten inches falls short of a twelve-inch measure, and the phrase also means on the ground beneath one's feet.

clue.text: Offer unexpected visitor bathroom facility

parts.note: an offer at auction is a bid
ET is the extra-terrestrial of the film, a most unexpected visitor

explanation.surface: Someone tries to sell a surprise guest a fixture for the bathroom.
explanation.walkthrough: ET, the alien of Spielberg's film, makes the 'unexpected visitor'.
explanation.definitionFit: A low basin for washing, found in many European bathrooms.

clue.text: Basketball shot you finally play badly

indicators.note: badly says the letters are jumbled, put in a poor order
finally picks the last letter of the word you

explanation.surface: A coach tells a basketball player their shooting is dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives U, the last letter of 'you'; 'badly' rearranges U with PLAY.
explanation.definitionFit: In basketball, a close-range one-handed shot bounced off the backboard.

clue.text: Emerge but just fail to get a medal, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear says the phrase is judged by how it sounds when spoken

parts.words: just fail to get a medal
parts.note: finishing fourth, one place behind bronze, misses the medals

explanation.surface: An athlete steps out after narrowly missing the podium, or so we are told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' signals that 'come fourth' sounds the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To come out into view, appear, as from a hiding place.

clue.text: Plant container that holds bird's food

definitions.meaning: a wild geranium, named for its beak-shaped fruit
a long-legged wading bird's beak, which holds its catch

explanation.definitionFit: A flowering geranium relative whose seed pod looks like a beak, and literally the beak of a wading bird.

clue.text: Where ball is placed for penalty without any delay

definitions.text: Where ball is placed for penalty

explanation.definitionFit: Footballers put the ball on the penalty mark, and the phrase also means immediately.

clue.text: Packaged underwear provided by Einstein?

parts.note: a bra is underwear
packaged means in box

explanation.surface: A great physicist supplies boxed lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark shows Einstein is an example of a clever person.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a very clever person, a genius.

clue.text: The bard's expressed wishes benefiting those who come after?

definitions.meaning: the bard is Shakespeare, whose first name is the answer; the 's stands for is

definitions.text: expressed wishes benefiting those who come after
definitions.meaning: a legal testament leaving property to heirs

explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's first name, and the legal document naming heirs to an estate.

clue.text: What one may need to get through at breakfast

definitions.text: What one may need to get through at breakfast

parts.words: What one may need to get through at breakfast
parts.note: the thing a spoon must crack to reach a boiled egg, not a pile of food to eat through

explanation.definitionFit: The brittle outer casing of a boiled egg must be broken to eat it.

clue.text: Not all in feast imbibed wine

indicators.note: Not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Not everyone at the banquet drank the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A sparkling white from Piedmont in Italy.

clue.text: Thinking about the future, dither with fags — dicey!

indicators.note: dicey, risky and uncertain, says the letters fall into a chancy new order

explanation.surface: A smoker hesitates with their cigarettes, a risky habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fags' is British slang for cigarettes; 'dicey' rearranges DITHER and FAGS together.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing good judgment about what lies ahead; prudent and planning well.

clue.text: Distinguished old female has upset public school

indicators.note: upset, in a down clue, says the school's name is turned upside down

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: An elderly lady overturns a posh school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ETON over; in Britain a 'public school' is an elite private one.
explanation.definitionFit: Notable, eminent, worth attention.

clue.text: Hesitation to put in barricade? This one could keep wild animals out

definitions.text: This one could keep wild animals out

indicators.note: to put in says the hesitation sound goes inside the barricade word

parts.note: a barricade is a defence
ER is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A hesitant builder wonders about a barrier to keep beasts away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to put in' places the hesitation sound inside the barricade word; the question mark warns that 'barricade' is only part of the wordplay, while the definition is the final sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall barrier around parkland, built so that stags and does cannot get in or out.

clue.text: Ecstasy is threefold round this host making his briefest appearance

indicators.note: round says the three ecstasy letters surround the short host abbreviation

parts.note: E is ecstasy, the drug, taken three times
the host in his shortest form, MC for master of ceremonies

explanation.surface: A drug-fuelled presenter puts in a fleeting appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' has the three ecstasy letters wrap the host's shortest form, so one E stands before and two after; 'making his briefest appearance' means the host abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: A compere introducing acts at a show.

clue.text: Beer brought on board in commercial exchanges

indicators.note: brought, with on board, says the beer is carried inside the ship's letters

parts.note: on board means aboard a steamship, SS, whose letters wrap the beer
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A trader loads beer onto a ship for business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' is a crossword convention: put a word inside SS, a steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: Transactions in which goods change hands for money.

clue.text: Strip of wood one provided as weapon

parts.note: a lath is a thin strip of wood
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A lone slat of timber serves as a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: A lathi is a heavy bamboo stick used by Indian police.
explanation.definitionFit: A long iron-bound bamboo club carried in South Asia.

clue.text: Unoriginal material turning yellow

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric

indicators.note: turning says the yellow word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: OR is the heraldic tincture gold, yellow

explanation.surface: Someone notes old fabric going yellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' looks like part of the definition, but it gives REP; 'turning' makes OR into RO.
explanation.definitionFit: A short form of reproduction, describing furniture or prints copied from older models.

clue.text: Source of notes and gold — treasure box brought by artist

parts.note: OR is gold in heraldry
a chest holds treasure
RA, Royal Academician, is a British artist

explanation.surface: A pirate's hoard and a painter's work combine in a tale of riches.
explanation.definitionFit: Musicians playing together in a large ensemble produce the music.

clue.text: It's glossy and offers a sort of appeal for adolescents

parts.note: SA is sex appeal
teen describes what is aimed at young people, as in teen fiction

explanation.surface: Something shiny has the kind of allure that attracts teenagers.
explanation.definitionFit: A cotton fabric woven to have a smooth shiny face like satin.

clue.text: The man will face female anger, the worst possible punishment

parts.note: the man will is he'll
ire is anger

explanation.surface: A man is about to meet a woman's wrath, the ultimate penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: The eternal flames of damnation are the severest penalty imaginable.
